verdict: OK to lend in Gorakhpur cement — back the grinding and trading units tied to GIDA and eastern-UP construction demand, structure tightly around fuel-cost pass-through and receivable discipline, and decline pure commodity clinker plays with stretched creditors.
title: Gorakhpur Cement: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Cement here is a grinding-and-blending business that turns clinker, gypsum and fly ash into bags sold through dealers into local construction.** Cash comes in from dealer sales, often on 30-60 day terms, while fuel (pet coke, imported coal) and power are paid faster — so the working-capital cycle is a permanent cash sink. Pricing power is thin: peers show blended NSR flat QoQ as premium share offset weak cement pricing [7]. **So when a proposal lands, check the split between trade (dealer) and institutional sales; if institutional share is rising, ask why — peers are curtailing low-margin institutional volumes [7].**

## What has changed now
**Volumes are strong but margins are squeezed.** JSW Cement's Q2 FY27 cement volumes rose 39.5% YoY to 2.29 million metric tons, with North utilisation up from 55% to 75% [4]; the trade press expects strong Q2 volumes but fuel costs weighing on margins [5]. Orient Cement ran ~14% EBITDA margin at INR770 per tonne [6]. **So when a proposal lands, check the fuel-cost pass-through clause in dealer contracts; if absent, ask how the unit absorbed the last pet-coke spike.**

## The Gorakhpur read
**Local sources are political, not financial.** The CM cites GIDA as an investment hub with ~50,000 jobs over a decade and names cement factories among new industries [1][2][3] — but no plant-level output, price or capacity data for Gorakhpur exists in these sources. **Lean on first principles plus peers: treat GIDA-linked grinding units and dealer networks as the real opportunity, and collect from customer all plant-level tonnage, fuel mix and receivable days.**

## How to grow safely
**Pursue grinding units and established dealer-finance borrowers serving eastern-UP construction; avoid pure clinker traders and units with stretched creditors.** Rating reports show stressed players meeting repayments by stretching creditors and adding debt [11], and group-company exposure draining cash [10]. **Take monthly: fuel invoices, dealer ageing, and a stock-and-receivable statement; covenant a maximum institutional-sales share and a fuel-cost pass-through clause.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Dealer receivable days rising month-on-month (monthly) -> freeze fresh limits and inspect dealer stock.**
- **Fuel cost per tonne climbing without a price revision (monthly) -> ask for the pass-through evidence or trim exposure.**
- **Creditor days stretching beyond terms (quarterly) -> treat as a liquidity signal, per peer precedent [11].**
- **Institutional sales share breaching covenant (monthly) -> reprice or exit.**

cost up, price flat -> demand pass-through proof or trim
stretch beyond terms -> liquidity flag, reduce exposure
